stem: A patient previously received a hormonal contraceptive prescription directly from a Massachusetts pharmacist. The applicable follow-up period has now elapsed, and the patient cannot provide the required evidence of a clinical visit. The patient asks the pharmacist to issue another prescription anyway. Which response best fits the statutory pathway?

choices.text: Issue another pharmacist prescription because a prior pharmacist prescription permanently waives follow-up requirements.
Switch to an injectable contraceptive so the clinical-visit requirement no longer matters.
Do not repeat the pharmacist prescribing pathway when the required post-prescribing clinical-visit evidence is absent after the applicable period.
Treat the missing clinical-visit evidence only as an insurance problem and prescribe normally.
Have a technician override the screening record because the patient previously tolerated the medication.

explanation.core_reasoning: The pharmacist-access statute pairs initial access with a follow-up safeguard. After a prior pharmacist prescription, the pharmacist cannot simply repeat prescribing when the required evidence of a clinical visit is missing after the applicable timeframe.

choice_analysis.A: Prior pharmacist prescribing creates the follow-up issue rather than a permanent waiver.
choice_analysis.B: Changing dosage form does not create authority outside the covered pathway or erase its conditions.
choice_analysis.C: This applies the statutory limit on repeat pharmacist prescribing when the required clinical-visit evidence is absent.
choice_analysis.D: The requirement is part of the prescribing framework, not merely a payer condition.
choice_analysis.E: A technician cannot waive a statutory or protocol condition based on prior tolerance.

related_facts: The statute requires a self-screening risk assessment before pharmacist prescribing.
The follow-up clinical-visit safeguard applies to repeat access after a pharmacist-issued prescription.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not remember only the access expansion; remember the condition that governs repeat pharmacist prescribing.

reasoning_steps: Recognize this is repeat pharmacist prescribing rather than first access
Identify that the follow-up period has elapsed

final_adjudication.adjudicator: GPT-5.6-Sol editor after independent audit A/B
final_adjudication.notes: Wave 1 admission after independent current-hash legal A/B KEEP/YES and realism A KEEP/PASS.
